Maya (CS): Quick convo to build a 1-page customer playbook: prefill vs on-demand + simple troubleshooting + renewal signals. want something concise for kickoff.
Alejandro (Solutions): Keep it copy-paste friendly. bullets + one tiny config snippet.
Sasha (Eng): Include recommended batch windows and when to enable streaming. also add a dev note on KV keys.
Maya (CS): Draft bullets: 1) Prefill for predictable prompts (TTL 1h default). 2) For short interactive sessions, use client debounce + short server batch (30-80ms). 3) Streaming = good for long responses/typing UX; off for micro calls.
Jin (PM): Add renewal-risk signals: >40% drop in active sessions over 14d = CS follow-up; no onboarding callbacks recorded in 7d = outreach.
Alejandro (Solutions): Example config to paste to customers:
```yaml
prefetch: { enabled: true, ttl_seconds: 3600 }
client: { debounce_ms: 150 }
server_batch: { max_wait_ms: 50, max_batch_tokens: 2048 }
streaming: { enabled_for_long_responses: true }
```
Sasha (Eng): Implementation notes: - debounce prevents duplicate requests from clients - batch window tradeoff: 30-80ms favors latency, 80-200ms favors cost. - KV cache key should include tenant-id + prompt-hash + schema-version.
Maya (CS): Can we ship this as "recommended defaults" in the 0-90 day onboarding packet?
Alejandro (Solutions): Yes. For enterprise mention dedicated capacity and shorter TTLs for PII workloads. add a one-sentence cost tradeoff note for hosted tier.
Jin (PM): I'll link to the renewal playbook and add exact thresholds.
Maya (CS): Feedback capture: quick 3-question template to send at 7 days post-go-live: 1) model relevance (1-5) 2) latency good? y/n 3) anything weird? (short) keep it <60s.
Sasha (Eng): Troubleshooting snippet for bursty drops (check queue/backpressure):
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/{id}/metrics?window=5m" | jq '.throughput, .latency_p95'
```
Maya (CS): Ops-bot deploy note?
ops-bot: deploy/finished cs-prefill-playbook-v0.1 by alejandro at 2024-04-11T16:45:12Z :white_check_mark:
Maya (CS): Last asks: Sasha, 2-line dev note about streaming cost overhead please.
Sasha (Eng): 2-liner: "Streaming keeps connections open and slightly increases per-request CPU; recommended for responses >300 tokens or interactive typing UX. For <100-token calls prefer non-streaming to reduce CPU and cost."
Maya (CS): Perfect. I'll attach the snippet and 3-question template to the onboarding guide and bring it up in enablement tomorrow. :sparkles:
